diagram_previews.alt: A regular hexagon with side sqrt3 and six pink petals, one on each side: each petal is a large circular segment bulging outwards, and neighbouring petals touch at the vertices of the hexagon.

The hexagon with its six pink petals; the dashed circles of the petals on the adjacent sides AB and BC have centres O1 and O2; the red segment O1O2 passes through the common vertex B, where the two circles touch; the blue radius O1A = 1, the red radius O1B = 1, the midpoint M of AB with a right-angle mark, and the dashed line from the centre O through M to O1.

difficulty_rationale: One must use the tangency of the equal petal circles at the common vertex (centres collinear with it, on opposite sides) to locate the circles, and then see that each petal is the larger segment of its disc.
